    Anos Coin Guard¶

    [!INFO] The Ledger Guard — Paper Over Gold, Steel Behind Paper Venner weighs. Anos counts — and the Coin Guard makes the count hold.

    History¶

    The military-commercial guard of the Anos Plutocracy — the counting-house oligarchy of South Erisdar that broke from the Kingdom of Tiphar in 158 AGD alongside Tiphar's other heirs (Scarlet Order, Grimmel) and built a global ledger instead of a kingdom. Where Venner built a channel, Anos built receipts: thin copper plates stamped A₥, redeemable against ledgers in the basalt towers of Anos city, backed not by metal but by trade volume — grain from Temas and Citrea, metals from Marti, timber from Lumina.

    The Coin Guard is the reason those receipts do not flutter away. Chartered by the council of ruling families under Carolas II's predecessors as the Guard of the Counting-Houses, it escorts grain fleets, garrisons colonial ports, and — when the ledger says a debtor has miscounted — arrives to help him recount. Its companies are recruited from the sons of clerks and the daughters of harbor masters, promoted for arithmetical talent as much as courage; a Coin Guard captain who cannot spot a false manifest is not long a captain.

    The Guard's most storied action is not a battle but a blockade-running in the Greater Ocean during a Venner interdiction — a convoy that scattered, reassembled by counting-house signals, and delivered Martian Drum hides and Kobran Gear steel to Anos Marti under Venner noses. Anos chronicles record it by tonnage.

    Patron¶

    The Anos council of plutocrats — the families who elect the head of the Anos from among themselves — and operationally the counting houses as institutions. Guardsmen swear on the ledger, not a relic: a hand on the bound book, oath that the number written is the number honored. Breach of oath is tried as forgery, which in Anos is worse than desertion.

    Relations: the Limese League plays Anos against Venner and the Guard knows it; the Guard's liaison in Lima grins and offers the League better rates anyway, because the game requires both players.

    Sigil¶

    A copper plate stamped A₥ on a slate-black field, crossed behind by two white quills — the Crossed Quills. Counting-house detachments render the A₥ in polished copper leaf that tarnishes honestly; campaign variants render it in chalk so it can be re-stamped after every audit. Commanders add a small Sousu pearl at the plate's corner when detached to Kreb or Megrel — pearls from Meble pay for discretion.

    Role¶

    Counting-house security, colonial garrison, and trade-route enforcement. The Coin Guard fields marines, escorted factor columns, and the ledger cavalry — mounted clerks who can ride to a Dissenbarg port like Komme or Tatak (Tatak joined Anos willingly, for profit; Komme by the ~542 AGD pact to liberate Taberis), audit a warehouse in an afternoon, and ride out with the shortfall or a mortgage on the town.

    It holds Anos's global span: Lumina Outpost in Lumina, Xeti Outpost in Xeti, New Kolorad on Kumir, Anos Maloca and Arrow of Anos in Merratodoni, Kolorad off Meble, and the Dissenbarg cities that still fly Anos colors because the ledger says they do.

    Relation to Currencies & Regions¶

    The Guard is the steel behind Anosi Mark — A₥ on copper, promise that a clerk in basalt will honor the number. When Venner blockades the Greater Ocean, the Mark wobbles; when the Guard convoys grain through, it firms. The Guard's pay-chest moves as ledger entries first, plates second — the final settlement always in a counting house, not a field tent.

    For foreign dealings it converts to Vennerian Ducat at Beast's Bay and Demon's Horn (grudgingly), to Dissenbarg Krona in Dissenbarg (weighing every city Krona on its own scales), to Meblean Pearl via Sousu at Kreb for Marti metals, and to Martian Drum hides at Anos Marti for herd wealth — the whole network rendered as one ledger spread that, miraculously, usually balances.
